title: Finishing the مُضَارِع Drills, then Reviewing Lesson One: إِنَّ and Its Six Sisters, ذُو, and أَمْ
summary: The first half completes the tamrīnāt on page 92, correcting sentences and choosing the right مُضَارِع form for each context, including the exception where a verb placed before a plural doer stays singular. The class then sets a test date and begins revising from lesson one: إِنَّ with its six sisters and the fatḥa they place on the مُبْتَدَأ, the difference between a verbal and a nominal sentence, ذُو as the possessor of something, أَمْ for alternative questions, and the rule that مِائَة and أَلْف take a singular counted noun.
key_points: When the verb comes before a plural doer it stays singular, even where instinct says otherwise — the exception that made several of the correction exercises tricky.

إِنَّ has six sisters — أَنَّ، كَأَنَّ، لَكِنَّ، لَيْتَ، لَعَلَّ — called sisters because they share one grammatical rule: they put the مُبْتَدَأ into the accusative, as in إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ, where اللَّهَ is the مُبْتَدَأ carrying the fatḥa.

A جُمْلَة فِعْلِيَّة (jumlah fiʿliyyah : verbal sentence) has فِعْل، فَاعِل، مَفْعُول and no مُبْتَدَأ or خَبَر; a جُمْلَة اسْمِيَّة (jumlah ismiyyah : nominal sentence) has مُبْتَدَأ (subject) and خَبَر (predicate). خَبَر means information, as it does in Urdu — the sky is the مُبْتَدَأ and blue is the خَبَر.

When a ضَمِير (ḍamīr : pronoun) attaches directly to إِنَّ or one of its sisters — إِنَّكَ، لَعَلَّكِ — the fatḥa rule no longer shows, because the pronoun is itself the مُبْتَدَأ and pronouns do not change form.

لَعَلَّ (laʿalla) means perhaps. It can carry تَرَجِّي (tarajjī : hope) or إِشْفَاق (ishfāq : apprehension), depending on the speaker — perhaps it will rain is hope for a farmer and apprehension for someone wanting to play outside.
ذُو (dhū) means the possessor or owner of something and is always مُضَاف, so the following word takes a kasra: ذُو خُلُقٍ, a possessor of good character. خُلُق is the singular of أَخْلَاق.
ذُو changes shape with its case — ذُو with ḍamma, ذَا with fatḥa, ذِي with kasra — and has the plural ذَوُو, the feminine singular ذَاتُ, and the feminine plural ذَوَاتُ.

To offer a choice rather than ask yes or no, open with هَمْزَة الِاسْتِفْهَام and use أَمْ: أَأَنْتَ مِنْ بَاكِسْتَانَ أَمْ مِنَ الْهِنْدِ. The general word for or is أَوْ; أَمْ belongs specifically to this questioning pattern.
أَمْ (or) is easily confused with أَمَّا (as for) — two different words.
Prices take the بَاء: بِكَمْ هَذَا, answered بِـ plus the amount. غَالِي (ghālī) is expensive and رَخِيص (rakhīṣ) is cheap; فَقَط (faqaṭ) means only; كَمْ puts the following word in the accusative.
Both إِنِّي and إِنَّنِي occur in the Qur'ān and mean the same thing — the extra nūn only eases pronunciation.
مِائَة (one hundred) and أَلْف (one thousand) take their counted noun in the singular — مِائَةُ رَجُلٍ، أَلْفُ رَجُلٍ — unlike the numbers three to ten, which take a plural.

Vocabulary: مَحَطَّة (station or stop) with نَزَلَ (to get off or descend), آخِر (last) as in الصَّفُّ الْآخِرُ, صَفّ (row), ثَانَوِيَّة (secondary school), and الْقَادِم (the coming or next), usable as الْمَحَطَّة الْقَادِمَة، السَّنَة الْقَادِمَة.
A مُضَاف can never carry أل, which is how the class ruled out one proposed answer.
questions: [00:08:00] Q: I thought nothing was wrong with that sentence — is it because of the word order? — A: Yes: when the doer follows the verb, the verb stays singular even if the doer is plural, so the plural verb had to be corrected back to singular.
[00:11:00] Q: Does آخِر occur in the Qur'ān? — A: الْآخِر occurs there with the same meaning; آخِر is also in common use in Arabic, and here it gives الصَّفُّ الْآخِرُ, the last row.

[00:17:00] Q: Does this deeper grammatical material come up in the Qur'ān? — A: For a basic understanding of the Qur'ān it is not needed; it matters only for a detailed grammatical breakdown, so it was left out at this level.
[00:26:00] Q: What is the grammatical rule shared by إِنَّ and its sisters? — A: They place a fatḥa on the مُبْتَدَأ of the sentence — usually, though not always, the word immediately following.
[00:30:05] Q: Should لِأَنَّ be counted as a seventh sister? — A: No, it is just أَنَّ with the lām attached, giving the meaning because.
[00:30:05] Q: When we revise, do we reread the whole lesson or only the main ideas? — A: Read through it and see what you pick up, concentrating on the main points.
[00:35:00] Q: Was ذُو introduced in the previous book or here? — A: Here, in this lesson.
[00:36:00] Q: What does انْتِقَام mean in إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ ذُو انْتِقَامٍ? — A: Retribution, revenge, or punishment in this context.
[00:38:00] Q: Isn't أَمْ related to أَمَّا? — A: No — أَمَّا means as for, while أَمْ is or in an alternative question. They are easy to mix up.

quiz.q: What single rule makes إِنَّ، أَنَّ، كَأَنَّ، لَكِنَّ، لَيْتَ and لَعَلَّ sisters?
options: They all place a fatḥa on the مُبْتَدَأ
They all take a verb after them
They all give the following word a kasra
quiz.a: The teacher defined the family by its shared rule: each puts the مُبْتَدَأ into the accusative, as in إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ.

quiz.q: In الْكِتَابُ جَدِيدٌ preceded by إِنَّ, which word takes the fatḥa?
quiz.a: الْكِتَاب is the subject being spoken about, so إِنَّ الْكِتَابَ جَدِيدٌ — the خَبَر is left untouched.

quiz.q: What does خَبَر mean in this grammatical sense?
options: The information given about the subject, the predicate
quiz.a: The teacher drew on Urdu, where خَبَر means news: it is the information given about the مُبْتَدَأ, as blue is about the sky.

quiz.q: Why is there no visible fatḥa in لَعَلَّكَ?
options: Because لَعَلَّ is not a true sister of إِنَّ
Because the attached pronoun is itself the مُبْتَدَأ and pronouns do not change form
Because لَعَلَّ gives a kasra instead
quiz.a: With a ضَمِير attached, the rule has nowhere to show — the pronoun's form stays fixed whether it is كَ or كِ.

quiz.q: What does لَعَلَّ mean, and what two senses can it carry?
quiz.a: The teacher's rain example: hope for the farmer, apprehension for the one hoping to play outside.

quiz.q: What does ذُو mean, and what does it do to the following word?
options: This — leaves the next word unchanged
Possessor of — it is مُضَاف, so the next word takes a kasra
From — gives the next word a fatḥa
Which — makes the next word definite
quiz.a: ذُو خُلُقٍ, a possessor of good character: ذُو is the مُضَاف and the following noun the مُضَاف إِلَيْهِ.

quiz.q: What is the feminine singular of ذُو?
quiz.a: ذَاتُ is the feminine singular, ذَوَاتُ the feminine plural, and ذَوُو the masculine plural.

quiz.q: Which word is used for or when a question offers two alternatives?
quiz.a: أَوْ is the general word for or, but in this question pattern with هَمْزَة الِاسْتِفْهَام the form used is أَمْ.

quiz.q: How does مِائَة differ from the numbers three to ten in what follows it?
options: It takes a plural counted noun, they take singular
It takes a singular counted noun, they take plural
quiz.a: مِائَةُ رَجُلٍ and أَلْفُ رَجُلٍ keep the counted noun singular, which is the one difference from the three-to-ten rule.

quiz.q: What is the difference in meaning between إِنِّي and إِنَّنِي?
options: There is no difference in meaning; the extra nūn only eases pronunciation
إِنِّي is used only with verbs
إِنَّنِي is used only in the Qur'ān
quiz.a: The teacher noted both appear in the Qur'ān and mean the same thing.

quran_examples.arabic: فَلَا تَحْسَبَنَّ اللَّهَ مُخْلِفَ وَعْدِهِ رُسُلَهُ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ ذُو انتِقَامٍ
quran_examples.transliteration: fa-lā taḥsabanna llāha mukhlifa waʿdihi rusulah, inna llāha ʿazīzun dhū intiqām
quran_examples.translation: So never think that Allah will fail in His promise to His messengers. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.
quran_examples.note: The teacher's own example for ذُو as possessor of something, and it also shows إِنَّ placing the fatḥa on اللَّهَ as the مُبْتَدَأ.

quran_examples.translation: And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
quran_examples.note: Cited in class as Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ being the possessor of great bounties; الْفَضْل takes a kasra as the مُضَاف إِلَيْهِ after ذُو.

quran_examples.arabic: إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدْنِي وَأَقِمِ الصَّلَاةَ لِذِكْرِي
quran_examples.transliteration: innanī anā llāhu lā ilāha illā anā fa-ʿbudnī wa-aqimi al-ṣalāta li-dhikrī
quran_examples.translation: Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.
quran_examples.note: The إِنَّنِي form of the pair the teacher mentioned, spoken to Mūsā عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام.

quran_examples.arabic: قُلْ إِنِّي أَخَافُ إِنْ عَصَيْتُ رَبِّي عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ
quran_examples.transliteration: qul innī akhāfu in ʿaṣaytu rabbī ʿadhāba yawmin ʿaẓīm
quran_examples.translation: Say: Indeed I fear, if I should disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.
quran_examples.note: The إِنِّي form the teacher paired with إِنَّنِي, showing both occur in the Qur'ān with the same meaning.

quran_examples.arabic: يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ وَالَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ
quran_examples.transliteration: yā ayyuhā al-nāsu uʿbudū rabbakumu alladhī khalaqakum wa-alladhīna min qablikum laʿallakum tattaqūn
quran_examples.translation: O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, that you may become righteous.
quran_examples.note: لَعَلَّكُمْ shows a sister of إِنَّ with a ضَمِير attached — exactly the case where the fatḥa rule stops being visible — and carries the sense of hope rather than apprehension.
